extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency information managers and policymakers responsible for implementing OMB Circular A-130 for scientific and technical information (STI)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for Federal agencies to manage, collect, preserve, disseminate, and provide public access to Scientific and Technical Information (STI) in compliance with OMB Circular A-130. Includes a template for agency implementation and recommendations for policy, standards, IT acquisition, evaluation, and interagency cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify "life-cycle planning" for information useability
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify “life-cycle planning” for information usability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redefine life-cycle planning to be better suited to information content management (not only systems/format), covering all aspects from initial planning through final disposition (permanent retention, retirement to archives, or destruction). Life-cycle should support varied agency missions and measure value differently for diverse user constituencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop guidelines to ensure information integrity for the public good
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop guidelines to ensure information integrity for the public good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clarity on assuring integrity and authenticity of STI (e.g., NLM’s practice of ensuring leased machine-readable data remain as accurate, complete, current, and accessible as direct NLM holdings through license agreements). Integrity measures should prevent degradation of life-critical information and preserve public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify guidance concerning public access to agency information
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify guidance concerning public access to agency information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clearer guidance to eliminate barriers to interagency and public use. Balance the public’s right to know with statutory protections (proprietary, privacy, national security). Use secondary dissemination channels (NTIS, Federal Depository Libraries, commercial vendors, agency web pages) and consider partial cost-recovery where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve conflicts between A-130 objectives and other Government initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolve conflicts between A-130 objectives and those of other Government initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and harmonize differences between A-130 guidance and other national and international STI requirements or initiatives to avoid contradictory policies and facilitate coherent agency implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor development of a selected mode of operation for Government information services
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor an effort to develop a selected mode of operation for Government information services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote a selected mode(s) of operation/standards for government information services to improve interoperability, reduce duplication, and promote consistent service models across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutionalize interagency cooperative efforts for information sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutionalize interagency cooperative efforts for information sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and sustain formal partnerships and exchange mechanisms (including multilateral international arrangements and barter where necessary) to leverage federallly funded STI and broaden access across agencies and with foreign partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Scientific and Technical Information (STI)
rubrics_metrics.description: STI derives primarily from research, development, and monitoring activities and includes text, numeric data, images, charts, graphs, metadata, methods and protocols, and formats from notebooks and preprints to formal publications and evaluated databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this working definition to set scope for what must be managed under agency STI programs; recognize multiple forms/media (print, micrographic, magnetic, optical) and informal interpersonal communications as part of the STI system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Template for Agency Implementation of OMB Circular A-130
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Template for Agency Implementation of OMB Circular A-130' was developed to help agencies identify and summarize information activities related to the Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should apply the template (and its accompanying clarifying questions) to gauge implementation progress, document practices, and identify areas needing additional guidance; Appendix B provides the template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate STI management into agency planning and budgeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Include requirements for management of information content (not just technology) in agency planning and budget processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STI objectives should be incorporated into mission statements, program plans, IRM budgets, and performance measures; agencies may centralize STI management or distribute responsibilities to program managers but must ensure content focus is planned and funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure collection and appropriate dissemination of Federally-funded STI
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies are generally responsible for ensuring STI resulting from Federally funded research and mission activities is received and appropriately disseminated (with exceptions for grantees expected to publish in peer-reviewed open literature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts and grants should contain provisions to ensure government access to knowledge (deliverables may include documents, databases, software). Agencies should establish processes to capture these deliverables and disseminate to intended audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track and monitor ongoing research to ensure information products are collected
rubrics_metrics.description: Some agencies maintain processes to track ongoing research so information products are collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement mechanisms (project tracking, monitoring) to ensure timely capture of STI deliverables tied to funded projects or contracts to avoid loss of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish procedures to control availability of statutorily-protected STI
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must establish procedures to control availability of certain statutorily protected STI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls must conform to laws, regulations, Executive Orders, international agreements, directives and agency policy; information may be withheld or restricted for specific periods or until regulatory changes permit release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with records management regulations and plan for retention/disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must comply with records management regulations and plan information disposition (permanent retention, retirement to archives, or destruction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because STI may remain useful indefinitely, agencies should establish retention policies and seek modern records management policies enabling use of current technologies for preservation and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participate in standards development to facilitate electronic STI management
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should be actively involved in standards (e.g., SGML, DIF, GILS) to facilitate management and processing of electronic STI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shared standards increase accessibility, timeliness, and completeness; examples include DOE’s promotion of SGML and NOAA’s use of DIF for data set catalogs; standards work supports interoperability and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt electronic collection and dissemination of technical reports and databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Shift from paper-based to digital collection and dissemination where practical (EDMS, electronic receipt, disks, CD-ROMs, Internet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transition may include scanning existing print while moving to native electronic submissions; implement systems (e.g., DTIC EDMS, DOE SGML efforts) to encompass electronic receipt, storage, retrieval, and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement quality assurance planning for numeric data programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality assurance planning is key for numeric data collection and integration (EPA EMAP emphasizes ISO 9000 and other QA tools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide guidance to data-contributing programs to structure collection approaches for cost-effectiveness, reduced burden, and higher quality; employ recognized QA standards where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce data collection burden through electronic systems (e.g., FastLane)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement electronic systems to reduce administrative burdens on data providers and researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: NSF FastLane for electronic proposal submission, status tracking, and award information. Agencies should collaborate on similar systems to streamline business processes with research communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure dissemination accommodates diverse user technology capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Make STI available in multiple formats to accommodate low-end and high-end user environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documents in electronic and paper formats as needed; design systems to support various access modes and legacy users while moving toward newer technologies (e.g., EDMS providing multiple formats).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop gateways, pointers, and centralized locator services (GILS, gateways)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide discovery tools (gateways, pointers, Government Information Locator Service) to lead end users to relevant sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement integrated services (e.g., Defense Gateway) and participate in GILS to improve findability and cross-agency discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish performance measurement and evaluation for STI services
rubrics_metrics.description: Use structured performance measurement and evaluation to manage STI programs (DTIC example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set measurable standards (response time, percentage of complaints, availability, reliability), capture production and cost data, use unit cost management, survey customer satisfaction, benchmark against best-in-business, and regularly review performance against goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop Web server standards and guidelines as a quality checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Create standards and guidelines for Web-based information services covering design, interface, and structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use human-interface and technical issue reviews, consult existing government/commercial/academic style guides, circulate drafts to implementors, continually revise as experience and technology evolve; use the document as an implementor checklist and intro for new managers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish management oversight for system reinvention projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide high-level oversight (committees/oversight groups) to direct and coordinate system reinvention/reengineering projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oversight groups should evaluate plans, approve milestones, review resource requirements, set priorities, coordinate transitions, and ensure customer feedback guides system development (NLM reinvention lab example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) solutions and benchmark private sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt an operating acquisition philosophy favoring off-the-shelf hardware and software ('invent nothing').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt commercially available, scalable products to meet requirements, modify only as necessary for government needs, and benchmark against private-sector practices to select appropriate tools (NTIS, NASA, FedWorld examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt licensing and pricing policies consistent with statutory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When providing STI via fee or license (e.g., NTIS), ensure pricing and licensing comply with statutory requirements and A-130 guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NTIS applies a marginal pricing philosophy to operations to recover costs; agencies leasing data to vendors should use license agreements to ensure leased data remain accurate, complete, current, and accessible (NLM practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance protection of information with accessibility to support mission/user needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance the public’s right to know against the government's need to protect proprietary, privacy, and national security information, while preserving information integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret protective actions in context of mission. If protection is necessary to ensure integrity or continued foreign information exchange, such protections should not be considered restrictive practices. Agency mission and user needs must drive deployment of information management resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop uniform approaches to information access and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Need for uniform approaches to information access and content across agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote consistent content and access standards to eliminate barriers to interagency and public use, increasing interoperability and facilitating broader reuse of the national STI resource.
